title: German Chancellor Faces Growing Pressure After Election Losses
subtitle: Friedrich Merz vows to continue his reform agenda despite calls for him to step down.

summary.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is facing a difficult political situation following poor results for his party in recent state elections. The far-right AfD party and the far-left Die Linke party both achieved significant gains in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin. Despite calls for his resignation, Merz has stated he will remain in office to lead his coalition government. He argues that his reform agenda is necessary for the country's democratic future. Political analysts are watching closely to see if his leadership can survive this period of instability.
summary.zh: 德國總理梅爾茲在近期邦選舉中表現不佳後，面臨艱難的政治局勢。極右派的德國另類選擇黨與極左派的左派黨在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦與柏林皆取得顯著斬獲。儘管外界要求他辭職，梅爾茲已表示將留任以領導聯合政府。他主張其改革議程對於國家的民主未來至關重要。政治分析家正密切關注他的領導地位能否度過這段動盪時期。

paragraphs.en: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is facing intense pressure to justify his leadership after his party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), suffered major losses in two state elections. On Sunday, voters in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and the city of Berlin delivered results that have shaken the national political landscape. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU failed to reach the 5% threshold required to enter the state parliament, a result described by Merz as a "disaster." Meanwhile, in Berlin, the CDU finished behind the far-left Die Linke party.
paragraphs.zh: 德國總理梅爾茲 (Friedrich Merz) 正面臨巨大的壓力，必須為其領導地位辯護，因為他的所屬政黨基督教民主黨 (CDU) 在兩場邦選舉中慘敗。週日，梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦與柏林市的選民投下的結果，震撼了全國的政治版圖。在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦，基民黨未能達到進入邦議會所需的百分之五門檻，梅爾茲將此結果形容為一場「災難」。與此同時，在柏林，基民黨的得票率落後於極左派的左派黨 (Die Linke)。

paragraphs.en: These defeats come only two weeks after the CDU experienced another significant loss in the state of Saxony-Anhalt. According to BBC News, Merz has faced mounting pressure since these results were announced, with some critics suggesting he could be replaced before his term ends. Despite these calls, Merz held a news conference on Monday to confirm that he has no intention of resigning. He stated that he is determined to keep his ruling coalition together for the sake of Germany's "democratic future."
paragraphs.zh: 這些挫敗發生在基民黨於薩克森-安哈特邦遭遇另一場重大失利僅僅兩週之後。根據英國廣播公司新聞網 (BBC News) 報導，自這些結果公布以來，梅爾茲面臨的壓力與日俱增，一些批評者認為他可能在任期結束前就會被撤換。儘管有這些呼聲，梅爾茲仍在週一召開記者會，確認他無意辭職。他表示，為了德國的「民主未來」，他決心維持執政聯盟的團結。

paragraphs.en: Merz acknowledged that the election results were a "heavy blow" for his party. However, he pushed back against the idea that his personal popularity was the only reason for the losses. "The reasons for these election results go far beyond my own person," he said, as reported by The Guardian. He suggested that Germany is witnessing a profound transformation of its political party system, similar to changes happening in other countries around the world. He remains committed to his federal agenda of tax and welfare reforms, which he describes as necessary to protect the country from authoritarianism.
paragraphs.zh: 梅爾茲承認選舉結果對他的政黨而言是「沉重的一擊」。然而，他反駁了關於他個人聲望低迷是導致敗選唯一原因的說法。根據《衛報》(The Guardian) 報導，他表示：「導致這些選舉結果的原因遠遠超出了我個人的因素。」他認為德國正見證其政黨體系深刻的轉型，這與世界其他國家正在發生的變化類似。他仍致力於推動聯邦層級的稅務與福利改革，並稱這些改革對於保護國家免受威權主義侵害是必要的。

paragraphs.en: The election results have highlighted the rising influence of parties on the political edges. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party won the most votes, securing 38% of the total. While the AfD is unlikely to form a government because other parties refuse to work with them, their success has caused significant concern. According to NPR News, the AfD’s co-leader Alice Weidel has been vocal about her belief that Merz will not remain in office for much longer. She claimed that the more Merz tries to stay in power, the more his party will suffer.
paragraphs.zh: 選舉結果凸顯了政治邊緣政黨日益增長的影響力。在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦，極右派的德國另類選擇黨 (AfD) 贏得了最多選票，總得票率達百分之三十八。雖然德國另類選擇黨不太可能組成政府，因為其他政黨拒絕與其合作，但他們的成功已引起了極大關注。根據美國公共廣播電台 (NPR News) 報導，德國另類選擇黨的共同領導人魏德爾 (Alice Weidel) 直言不諱地表示，她認為梅爾茲不會再留任太久。她聲稱，梅爾茲越是試圖保住權力，他的政黨就會受到越大的傷害。

paragraphs.en: In Berlin, the situation is also changing. The far-left Die Linke party, led by Elif Eralp, won the most votes. Eralp has promised to address the city's rent crisis by introducing a rent cap and potentially taking ownership of housing units from large private landlords. This proposal is expected to be a major point of discussion as the party begins negotiations to form a new coalition government. A coalition is an agreement between two or more political parties to work together to govern, which is often necessary in Germany’s electoral system when no single party wins a majority.
paragraphs.zh: 在柏林，局勢也在改變。由艾拉普 (Elif Eralp) 領導的極左派左派黨贏得了最多選票。艾拉普承諾透過引入租金上限，並可能從大型私人房東手中收購住宅單位，來解決該市的租屋危機。隨著該黨開始協商組成新的聯合政府，這項提案預計將成為討論的重點。聯合政府是指兩個或多個政黨為共同執政而達成的協議，在德國的選舉制度中，當沒有單一政黨贏得多數席次時，這通常是必要的做法。

paragraphs.en: Although Merz has received support from powerful regional leaders within his own party, questions remain about how long this support will last. The position of chancellor is becoming increasingly difficult, with some observers calling it a "poisoned chalice"—a term used to describe a job that seems attractive but actually brings great trouble and hardship to the person who holds it. Merz has insisted that his reform plans require "backbone, steadfastness and patience," and he intends to demonstrate these qualities as he continues his work.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管梅爾茲已獲得黨內強大地方領袖的支持，但這種支持能持續多久仍是未知數。總理職位變得越來越難以勝任，一些觀察家稱其為「毒聖餐杯」，這個詞用來形容一份看似誘人，實則為擔任者帶來巨大麻煩與苦難的工作。梅爾茲堅持認為他的改革計畫需要「骨氣、堅定與耐心」，並打算在繼續工作時展現這些特質。

paragraphs.en: As the country looks toward the future, the stability of the current government remains a central concern. The SPD, which is the CDU’s partner in the federal coalition, is also navigating its own challenges. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the SPD state governor Manuela Schwesig is expected to lead a new government, having focused her campaign on acting as a barrier against the AfD. As the political landscape continues to shift, the ability of the federal government to implement its agenda will be tested. For now, Merz remains in office, determined to navigate what he calls a historic challenge for his country.
paragraphs.zh: 當國家展望未來之際，現任政府的穩定性仍是核心關切。作為基民黨在聯邦聯合政府中的夥伴，社會民主黨 (SPD) 也正應對自身的挑戰。在梅克倫堡-西波美拉尼亞邦，社民黨的邦總理施韋斯格 (Manuela Schwesig) 預計將領導新政府，她的競選重點在於作為抵禦德國另類選擇黨的屏障。隨著政治版圖持續變動，聯邦政府執行其議程的能力將受到考驗。目前，梅爾茲仍留任總理，決心帶領國家度過他所稱的歷史性挑戰。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To express disagreement with an idea or a plan.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 反對、抵制（某個想法或計畫）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於實體推擠，這裡指在意見上的反對。文中：However, he pushed back against the idea that his personal popularity was the only reason for the losses.

keyTerms.definitionEn: The extreme or radical parts of a political spectrum.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （政治光譜的）邊緣，指極端派系。
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指物體的邊緣，這裡指政治立場極端。文中：The election results have highlighted the rising influence of parties on the political edges.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A situation or position that seems desirable but actually brings great trouble.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 看似誘人實則帶來災難的職位或處境。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意為「有毒的聖杯」，比喻看似光鮮亮麗卻充滿麻煩的職位。文中：The position of chancellor is becoming increasingly difficult, with some observers calling it a "poisoned chalice"—a term used to describe a job that seems attractive but actually brings great trouble and hardship to the person who holds it.

quiz.question: What happened to the CDU in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania according to the text?

options.A: They finished behind the far-left Die Linke party.
options.B: They failed to secure enough votes to enter the state parliament.
options.C: They won the second-highest number of votes in the state.
options.D: They formed a new coalition government with the SPD.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。文章第一段明確指出，在 Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania，CDU 未能達到進入州議會所需的 5% 門檻，這被 Merz 稱為一場「災難」。選項 A 是關於柏林選區的結果；選項 C 與文章內容不符，因為該黨根本沒進議會；選項 D 錯誤，因為 SPD 在該州是尋求領導新政府，而非與 CDU 組閣。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might the AfD's recent success be considered particularly problematic for the CDU?

options.A: Because the AfD is planning to join the CDU in a federal coalition.
options.B: Because the AfD has already successfully replaced Merz as Chancellor.
options.C: Because the AfD is gaining power while other parties refuse to cooperate with them, complicating governance.
options.D: Because the AfD is the only party that supports Merz's tax and welfare reforms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。根據第四段，AfD 在 Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania 贏得 38% 的選票，但其他政黨拒絕與其合作，這意味著儘管 AfD 勢力大增，卻難以組建政府，這導致德國政治局勢更難以穩定。選項 A 與文意相反；選項 B 錯誤，Merz 尚未下台；選項 D 無根據，文中並未提到 AfD 支持 Merz 的改革。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what is the best meaning of the phrase 'poisoned chalice'?

options.A: A job that is highly prestigious but ultimately leads to failure.
options.B: A position that is dangerous due to physical threats.
options.C: A political role that requires illegal actions to maintain.
options.D: A task that is easy to perform but offers no financial reward.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 A。文章第六段解釋了「poisoned chalice」是指一個看起來很有吸引力（職位高），但實際上會給擔任者帶來極大麻煩與困境的工作。選項 B 錯誤，文中並未提到人身安全威脅；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未暗示非法行為；選項 D 錯誤，這並非輕鬆的工作，且重點在於其帶來的負面後果而非報酬。
